newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras says to issue shares to 1996 subscribers.
newsitem.headline: Telebras says to issue shares to 1996 subscribers.

text.p: Brazilian federal telecoms holding Telebras said it will distribute shares to telephone subscribers who acquired phone lines in 1996, reversing an earlier decision to pay them in cash.

Telebras' decision, announced in advertisements published in local newspapers, is part of an accord to capitalize line-purchase contracts fully paid last year and end the firm's so-called autofinancing program.
Under the program, new subscribers would receive shares of Telebras or its state-level operators in exchange for money paid to buy a telephone line.
The telecoms giant said in June it planned to simply refund the money to 1996 subscribers.
However, according to the ad, it now says those who bought a phone line last year will receive shares either of Telebras or its local operating subsidiary as originally promised.
Those who purchased lines before August 25, 1996 will receive shares equal to the amount originally paid, plus interest, divided by the December 31, 1996 book value of the stock, it said.
Those who bought lines after that date will get shares based on the market value at the time of the subsidiaries' planned capitalization if the market price is higher than book value.
Telebras said it will waive its preferential rights to the new shares of its subsidiaries so they may be distributed to the 1996 subscribers.

The capitalization accord, signed in June with the National Development Bank's investment arm BNDESPar, also made possible the collection of 110 million reais from the sale of its subscription rights to new shares of Telebras' units.
The accord also paved the way for the placement of shares of Telebras subsidiaries in stock markets.
A local newspaper Sunday quoted Telebras chief Fernando Xavier Ferreira as saying the firm planned to take public the 17 Telebras units that do not currently trade on local stock markets.

Telebras' preferred share is the benchmark issue on Brazilian stock markets and trades in New York as a Level Three American Depositary Receipt (ADR). It was not clear whether the subscribers would receive common or preferred stock.
